subject: One Global detection function, multiple levels of stratification

messages.author: 76223116e105ddbc
messages.subject: One Global detection function, multiple levels of stratification
parts:
Dear List,

I am struggling with a large and sprawling dataset and could use some=20
guidance on analysis. The data are line-transect visual detections strati=
fied by=20
study area (n=3D2) and collected during three time periods. I would like =
to=20
generate 6 density estimates for each of the 45 species in the dataset, o=
ne=20
estimate for each study-area-time-period. So far, I have estimated detect=
ion=20
functions for the 10 species that have obs > 60. I have assigned each of=
the=20
remaining 35 rare species (obs n =3D 2-20) to a "detection group" based o=
n their=20
similarities to more abundant species (following Alldredge et al 2007). M=
y plan=20
is to use the Multiplier to estimate densities for the rare species based=
on the=20
abundant species in their detection group. Now I am stalled out trying to=
=20
decide how to apply the global detection function to estimates for each s=
tudy-
area-time-period. The data are currently structured with Stratum =3D Stud=
y=20
Area, Sample =3D Time period, and Subsample =3D transect.=20

Options I am considering:
1. Separate Projects for each time period, use Study area to stratify.
2. Creating a single Stratum field that designates 6 strata, one for each=
study-
area-time-period.

The biggest problem is that one of the study areas has far fewer detectio=
ns=20
than the other one, so I need all the observations from both study areas =
to=20
generate a pooled detection function. There is little reason to suspect a=
=20
difference in detection rate between the study areas. Any advice on how t=
o=20
tackle this beast would be much appreciated.

Thanks!
Adrian
